ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a fixed-bias common-emitter transistor basic amplifier circuit. The base is connected to +VCC through a 200 kΩ resistor labeled Rb; the emitter is directly grounded; the collector is connected to +VCC through Rc=2 kΩ; the input terminal is connected to the base through coupling capacitor C1, and the output terminal is connected to load RL through coupling capacitor C2. Reasoning: When finding the quiescent base current, perform DC analysis. Coupling capacitors C1 and C2 are open-circuited for DC, so load RL and the input signal do not affect the base bias loop. The base DC loop satisfies KVL: VCC = IBQ·Rb + VBEQ. Given VCC=12 V, VBEQ≈0, Rb=200 kΩ, so IBQ=(12-0)/200 kΩ=12/200000 A=60×10^-6 A=60 μA.
